If the result is over the rider's Strength, they are thrown off before the Squig moves away, and take a Strength 2 hit with no Armour save as they crash to the ground. The rider is now dismounted for the rest of the battle. If the roll is equal to or below their Strength, the rider keeps their grip and remains atop the Squig.

notes: Multi-model mounts, allocation between rider and mount, and the throw-off test are outside the 1v1 duel; the KB record is an unimplemented placeholder.

clause_text: Ogres don't use daggers for fighting, just for eating. They don't carry them on the battlefield. If forced to, by losing a weapon or not carrying any weapon, they will fight unarmed. But since their physical strength the -1S penalty does not apply, but the +1 enemy armour save still does. They may make more than one unarmed attack, depending on their Attacks value. Note that you cannot combine this unarmed attack with another weapon, so it doesn't count as an additional attack like the dagger would. It can only be made if the ogre doesn't have any other weapons at his disposal.

The engine has an unarmed-without-penalties flag, but it also cancels the opponent's +1 armour save (the armour context removes the weapon's target bonus when that flag is set), which contradicts this print; wiring the flag as-is would therefore implement the rule wrongly. A separate effect that only drops the -1 Strength is required.

notes: Fully connected: _injury_context reads the tag, injury_condition converts a Knocked Down result to Stunned and the KB grants the skill to the Orc bands. The conversion happens where the hand-to-hand injury result is computed, which is what the printed rule describes; no gap identified.

semantic_contract: Instead of his normal attacks the bearer may make a single Strength 5 attack that hits automatically, ignores armour saves and cannot be parried; observable: one automatic hit that bypasses the armour save and the parry.
notes: All four parameters are consumed: automatic_hit in prepare_hit_context, fixed_strength in _attack_strength, ignore_armour in prepare_armour_context and the armour target, cannot_be_parried in resolve_parry; the item is declared as weapon.vomit-attack with that payload and the KB grants it to six Troll profiles. The one part not verified by reading is the trading of the normal attacks for this one, which the payload does not express; that stays a caller decision rather than a missing parameter here.

clause_text: A natural 6 to wound is critical unless a 6 was required.
semantic_contract: A close-combat wound roll of a natural 6 is a critical wound, unless the required To-Wound target is already 6. Closure: with target <=5 a rolled 6 sets critical, with target 6 it never does, and a successful rerolled wound is not critical (Devil's Toxin / Sure Strike).
notes: Contracted by resolve_wound (critical = rolled_success and target < 6 and roll >= threshold, and not rerolled). The "unless a 6 was required" exception is the target < 6 test; critical_on_reroll=False covers the Devil's Toxin rereoll clause. No gap found.

clause_text: A warrior causes at most one critical hit per close-combat phase.
semantic_contract: Within one close-combat phase a fighter may score at most one critical wound; later natural sixes in the same pool stay ordinary wounds. Closure: after the first critical the second natural 6 in the same pool resolves as a normal wound, and the allowance is restored in the next round.
notes: FighterState.critical_available is consumed on the first critical and restored by _start_round_state at the start of each round. Companion effects that consume separately (Spectral Touch extra wound, Black Lotus) do not spend a second allowance.

clause_text: Resolve the basic critical table on D6 with critical-table modifiers; all results cause two wounds, 3+ ignores armour, and 5+ adds two to Injury. For 1-2 save before doubling.
semantic_contract: The basic critical chart is a D6 plus critical-table modifiers: every result sets damage 2, a result of 3 or more ignores armour, a result of 5 or more adds +2 to the Injury roll, and results 1-2 leave armour and Injury untouched. Closure: resolve_critical rolls D6+modifier and returns damage 2 with ignore_armour for >=3 and injury_modifier 2 for >=5.
notes: resolve_critical implements exactly damage=2 / ignore_armour>=3 / injury+2>=5 with a caller-supplied modifier (Dark Elf Blade and Draich add critical_injury_bonus). The printed "save before doubling" ordering is the armour-before-damage order in _resolve_wound_damage. No gap; weapon-family charts are a separate ruleset and explicitly out of this operator.

clause_text: Use the higher damage instead of multiplying another multiple-wound effect.
semantic_contract: A critical doubling is never multiplied by another multiple-wound source; the larger of the two values is used. Closure: a Bloodroot (damage 2) critical hit inflicts 2 wounds, not 4.
notes: _resolve_wound_damage uses max(1, weapon_damage, critical.damage) — a maximum, not a product. Documented as the project composition of the printed "use the higher damage" instruction.

clause_text: Charge and other strike-first effects resolve before normal Initiative order.
semantic_contract: A charging fighter and any strike-first effect act before ordinary Initiative order; within the same priority tier the higher Initiative acts first, exact ties are decided without bias. Closure: the charger resolves its pool before a non-strike-first defender and ties fall back to Initiative then a random roll.
notes: resolve_priority raises the value to max(value, charging) only in the first round and keeps explicit strike-last weapons below it; first_acts_before compares (priority, initiative) and rolls on a tie.

clause_text: A warrior who stood up in the Recovery phase strikes last. This standing-up penalty applies only to the turn in which the warrior stood up.
semantic_contract: Standing up from Knocked Down in the Recovery phase sets priority to last for that turn only; an explicit strike-first ability overrides it. Closure: a stood-up fighter resolves after its opponent in that round and its priority returns to normal in the following round.
notes: resolve_priority sets value=-1 when context.stood_up and the fighter lacks skill.always-strikes-first, which is the "Lost Innocence" override; _start_round_state only stands a warrior up once, so the penalty is turn-scoped.

clause_text: Two one-handed weapons grant one additional Attack after other modifiers.
semantic_contract: Carrying two one-handed close-combat weapons adds exactly one Attack, applied after every other attack modifier (including doubling). Closure: a two-weapon fighter with A2 and Frenzy resolves 5 attacks, not 6.
notes: build_attacks adds extra_weapon_attack after the frenzy/ferocious doubling and the paired-weapon bonus is the same single extra attack, so a paired weapon does not pay twice.

clause_text: When weapons differ, choose one for a single attack and use the other for all remaining attacks.
semantic_contract: With two different weapons the off-hand contributes exactly one attack resolved with that weapon profile and all remaining attacks use the nominated main weapon; the additional-hand attack is not freely allocated. Closure: a sword+dagger fighter has one dagger-profile attack (target armour +1) and the rest as sword attacks.
notes: allocate_attack_weapons gives the off hand one attack and the rest to the main weapon. The printed "choose one for a single attack" freedom is realised as the main/off-hand nomination (F005 Shifty/paired rulings) rather than an arbitrary per-attack choice; recorded as a documented project reading, not a source change.

clause_text: Strikes first and has Concussion on Injury rolls of 2-4.
semantic_contract: Strike-first melee weapon whose injury roll of 2-4 is treated as Stunned. Closure: priority 1 in the first and later rounds and a 2-4 Injury total yields STUNNED.
notes: Printed profile equals the contract parameters; the compiled attack EffectSet is consumed by build_attacks and the hit/wound/armour/injury contexts. Concussion is consumed by _injury_context (injury_condition treats 2-4 as stunned); priority 1 by resolve_priority. Note the source prints Concussion for the Ankus while the sibling mace-family rule and the operator agree, so no conflict.

clause_text: An Arcane Candelabrum from a holy temple. Counts as a holy relic, brazier iron and lantern that is used one-handed.
semantic_contract: One-handed weapon that also counts as a holy relic, brazier iron and lantern. Closure: the attack carries attack.fire with ignition 5 and bearing the item grants defence.holy-relic.
notes: Printed profile equals the contract parameters; the compiled attack EffectSet is consumed by build_attacks and the hit/wound/armour/injury contexts. compile_fighter appends defence.holy-relic when the Arcane Candelabrum is carried and the contract carries attack.fire/ignition_threshold. Its "counts as brazier iron" identity is realised through the shared tags rather than a second weapon profile.

clause_text: The Beastmaster wielding a Beastlash causes Fear in animals, any animal charged or wishing to charge a Beastmaster with one of these weapons must first take a Fear test.
semantic_contract: A Beastlash bearer causes Fear against animal opponents only, and an animal that charges or is charged must take a Fear test. Closure: against an opponent carrying species.animal tags the bearer counts as Fear-causing and the animal resolves the ordinary Fear test; against non-animals it grants nothing.
notes: causes_fear implements the Beastbane Fear directly: it returns true when the enemy carries species.animal and any attacking weapon carries the weapon.beastlash tag, and its comment states that Beastbane belongs to a wielded weapon and affects animals only. The weapon-scoped, animal-only variant therefore already exists, and the earlier behaviour-gap note read only mechanic.causes-fear and missed the weapon-tag branch. The identity is the existing weapon.beastlash profile rather than a proposed new one.

clause_text: Whipcrack grants one bonus attack when charging or charged; only that bonus strikes first when charged, and two whips do not double it.
semantic_contract: A whip-tagged weapon grants exactly one bonus attack in the round it charges or is charged; when charged that attack strikes first, and carrying two whips never doubles the bonus. Closure: the whip pool gains one attack, the bonus attack resolves at strike-first priority when charged, and a second whip contributes only the ordinary additional-hand attack.
notes: whipcrack_weapon() accepts the steel-whip, beastlash, pirate-scourge and serpent-whip tags and apply_round_weapon_attack_modifiers adds a single point of attacks in the first round when charging or charged. Because the bonus is a pool-level +1 it is naturally capped at one for two whips. Recorded as related rather than equivalent because the whipcrack clause is a shared family behaviour keyed by tag, not an effect of the Beastlash profile alone.

clause_text: When attacking knocked down opponents, Misericordia bypasses all armor saves.

notes: prepare_armour_context accepts a static ignore_armour flag only; a condition-scoped armour denial has no parameter. The engine currently short-circuits a helpless target to out-of-action, which does not implement the printed armour clause, so a behaviour addition is required rather than a data connection. Correction round: the violation point and an observable example. The armour sequence in attacks._resolve_wound_damage builds prepare_armour_context from the attacker and defender states without any knocked-down test and passes only the static effect.ignore_armour flag into phases.resolve_armour, so a Knocked Down opponent still rolls its armour save before the helpless short-circuit sends it out of action. Distinguishing example: Misericordia against a Knocked Down target with a 4+ armour save - printed: no armour save is attempted and the wound stands; current: the 4+ save is rolled and can cancel the wound. A condition-scoped armour denial has no parameter in the contract (ArmourContext carries one ignore_armour flag), so the step is behaviour.
