The printed clause is optional ("may invoke") and the permanent duel-engine ruling retains the documented automatic Black Hunger activation convention (docs/decisions/design-rulings.md), so the passive tag is the decided behaviour, not a defect. The invocation and the one-turn duration are delivered by that convention; the missing map movement is recorded in its own clause and is not an admitted behaviour gap.

clause_text: For that turn he gains +1 Attack.
semantic_contract: While Black Hunger is active the bearer gains +1 Attack for that turn. Closure: the attack pool carries one extra attack from the mechanic tag.
notes: effect.attacks_bonus 1 is read by build_attacks for the passive mechanic tag, so the printed +1 Attack is delivered for the whole turn.

clause_text: At the end of the turn he suffers 1D3 Strength 3 hits with no armour save.
semantic_contract: At the end of the boosted turn the bearer suffers 1D3 Strength 3 hits that allow no armour save. Closure: D3 Strength 3 automatic hits resolve against the bearer with armour denied and no critical.
notes: _black_hunger rolls 1D3 (RollRequest(...,3)) and resolves each as an automatic, unparryable, armour-ignoring Strength 3 hit with no critical, which is the printed backlash. resolve_round runs it for both fighters once the round attacks finish, the end of the boosted turn under the retained activation convention and the printed D3 S3 unsaveable self-hits.

clause_text: And adds the result of 1D6 x 0.4" + 1" to his Movement.
semantic_contract: The printed 1D6 x 0.4" + 1" Movement addition belongs to the excluded tabletop movement subsystem; no duel operator is required and the mechanic keeps only its attack and backlash contributions.
notes: Recorded explicitly so the excluded half is visible and the closure never depends on map movement. No movement term exists in the duel state; its absence is not an admitted behaviour gap.

clause_text: Replaces charge attacks with one +1 Strength, +1 To Hit attack that critically wounds on 5+ and ignores weapon and skill modifiers.
semantic_contract: A charge may be resolved as one single attack at +1 Strength and +1 To Hit that wounds critically on 5+ and ignores weapon and skill modifiers. Closure: the whole pool is replaced by exactly one attack carrying S+1, +1 to hit and a critical threshold of 5, and no equipped-weapon or skill modifier reaches it.
notes: _resolve_attack_pool substitutes the pool with the body-slam EffectSet (strength_bonus 1, hit_modifier 1), build_attacks clamps the charging round to one attack, prepare_wound_context raises the critical threshold to 5 and _combined_effect returns the slam profile alone so global (skill) modifiers never merge into it. The printed "ignores weapon modifiers" is realised more strongly: the equipped weapon is replaced outright.

clause_text: Ogres learn to use their vast bulk in a charge, trampling the enemy to the ground. When charging, an Ogre with this skill may attempt a single attack with a +1 'to hit' modifier rather than making his normal attacks. If successful the enemy model is automatically knocked down.
semantic_contract: When charging, an Ogre may attempt a single attack at +1 To Hit instead of his normal attacks; a successful attack knocks the enemy model down automatically. Closure: the chosen charge resolves exactly one attack at +1 to hit and an unparried, unsaved hit leaves the defender Knocked Down without a To Wound roll.
notes: _resolve_attack_pool builds the single +1 hit attack; _resolve_reference_attack_once returns early for a bull-charge attack (the wound step is consumed by the handler) and the pool sets KNOCKED_DOWN when the hit is not parried and not saved. The printed "if successful" is read as an unparried, unsaved hit; that refinement of the printed wording is recorded here as the project reading.

clause_text: At own-turn start recover at most one lost wound on 5+, unaffected by fire. Requires Great Thirster.
semantic_contract: At the start of his own turn the bearer recovers at most one lost wound on a 5+, and the attempt is unaffected by fire. Closure: one 5+ attempt per own turn restores exactly one wound and cannot exceed the starting total.
notes: _revenant_recovery is one 5+ attempt per key, restores exactly one wound, respects the monstrous wound maximum and is independent of the fire-recovery branch. Relation kept "related" only because the printed "Requires Great Thirster" prerequisite is an eligibility/data coupling that nothing inside A verifies.

clause_text: Requires Great Thirster.
semantic_contract: The recovery operator may only be granted to a fighter that also carries Great Thirster. Closure: no figure is compiled with mechanic.curse-of-the-revenant unless the same figure carries mechanic.great-thirster.
notes: The prerequisite lives in the KB grant data, not in the operator: _revenant_recovery only tests for the recovery tag itself. Within block A the coupling could not be verified from the compiled data, so the first unresolved step is the data grant (recorded as work=data, not as a missing connection).

clause_text: Fierezza Heroes re-roll failed melee hits in the first combat round against enemy Heroes.
semantic_contract: Fierezza Heroes re-roll failed close-combat hits in the first combat round when fighting an enemy Hero. Closure: with both fighters Heroes and the Fierezza house declared, missed close-combat hits are re-rolled in the first round only.
notes: _hit_reroll raises pride only for first_round, requires an explicit house-guard.* declaration, resolves house-guard.fierezza with fighter-kind.hero and refuses to guess the opponent role (it raises instead). The printed house/role restrictions are therefore enforced as explicit inputs; the reroll itself is delivered.

clause_text: If fighting unarmed, the Hero may choose to reduce his Attacks by –1 and thus gain +1 Strength in close combat. The monk may sacrifice any number of attacks this way.
semantic_contract: Fighting unarmed, the monk may reduce his Attacks by one to gain +1 Strength in close combat and may sacrifice any number of attacks this way. Closure: for each attack given up while fighting with fists or natural attacks the attack Strength rises by one, and the pool and the Strength term move by the same amount.
notes: _attack_strength adds effect.energy_focus_attacks for fist and natural attacks while build_attacks removes the same number from the pool, and compile_fighter validates the energy-focus count through the characteristic block, so an out-of-range choice is refused instead of silently applied.

clause_text: Gains Frenzy after taking an enemy out of action; lost when knocked down, stunned or out of action.
semantic_contract: The fighter gains Frenzy after taking an enemy out of action, and loses it when he is knocked down, stunned or taken out of action. Closure: an out-of-action result against the opponent sets frenzy, and a knocked-down, stunned or out-of-action condition on the bearer clears it again.
parameters: {"grants": "frenzy", "lost_when": ["knocked down", "stunned", "out of action"], "trigger": "taking an enemy out of action"}
conditions: {"duration": "until the bearer is down, stunned or out", "trigger": "opponent out of action"}
notes: aftermath._react_to_wound sets frenzy when the defender is out of action and the bearer is standing, which delivers the grant, and the printed loss is delivered by the general injury transition rather than by a great-thirster term: attacks._resolve_wound_damage closes every damaging resolution with frenzy=defender_state.frenzy and condition == Condition.STANDING, so any injury outcome that leaves the bearer knocked down, stunned or out of action clears the flag. Recovery does not restore it - aftermath._start_round_state stands a knocked-down fighter up and resets parries, critical availability and attack penalties but never sets frenzy - so the flag stays clear until the bearer takes another enemy out of action. tests/python/combat/modular/test_local_modifier_variants.py::test_great_thirster_prerequisite_has_its_own_out_of_action_frenzy_effect exercises both directions through resolve_reference_attack. No separate great-thirster consumer is owed.

clause_text: A natural hit six wounds automatically and cannot be parried; armour and special saves remain allowed.
semantic_contract: A natural hit roll of six wounds automatically and cannot be parried, while armour and special saves remain available. Closure: a natural six on the To Hit roll skips the To Wound roll, the parry step is refused and the armour and special-save steps still resolve.
notes: _resolve_reference_attack_once raises the killing-blow branch on a natural six: the attack is made unparryable and the wound is automatic, while the armour and special-save steps run unchanged. The rule is rejected by require_optimized_support for the optimized ports, which is a port-scope limit and not a semantic gap of the modular operator.

clause_text: Some Amazon women develop their fighting motions into a graceful dance that can transfix their foes. Any model fighting in base contact with the Amazon must take a Leadership test at the start of each turn. If they fail they cannot attack that turn but may defend themselves. The dance however is useless against Lizardmen and undead who are immune to their charms.
semantic_contract: Any model in base contact must take a Leadership test at the start of each turn; on a failure it cannot attack that turn but may defend itself, and the dance is useless against Lizardmen and undead. Closure: each round the engaged opponent tests Leadership and a failure blocks only its attacks, and a Lizardman, undead or charm-immune opponent skips the test entirely.
parameters: {"failure": "cannot attack but may defend", "frequency": "start of each turn", "immune": ["Lizardmen", "undead"], "test": "Leadership"}
notes: resolve_round runs the dance from a combat-start snapshot with a Leadership test; on failure the target is charm_attack_blocked (attacks blocked, defence kept) and the gate exempts nature.undead, species.lizardman and mechanic.charm-immunity. "Each turn" is realised per duel round, which in a duel is the same time unit.

clause_text: The goblin is adept at using a net to disable his enemies. They learn their skill hunting wild cave squigs in the depths of the mountains. The technique he has mastered is 'chuck and charge'. The goblin may declare that he is making a net charge. He throws the net at a target in the same way as described in the Mordheim rulebook. If he hits and the target fails to escape the net then target counts as knocked down and the goblin completes his charge. If he misses or the target escapes then the goblin makes a failed charge. If the failed charge would take him into base contact then stop him 1" away. A warrior who is caught in a net will be automatically hit in combat. The goblin must still roll to wound just as with a knocked down enemy. In the warrior's next recovery phase, unless he is stunned or out of action he will cut himself out of the net but cannot do anything else and will go last in combat just as if he had stood up from being knocked down.
semantic_contract: A goblin may declare a net charge: if the net hits and the target fails to escape, the target counts as knocked down and the goblin completes his charge, the netted warrior is hit automatically in combat and must still be rolled To Wound as against a knocked-down enemy; in his next recovery phase he cuts himself free, cannot do anything else and goes last in combat as if he had stood up. Closure: a netted target is Knocked Down, is hit automatically, and its recovery phase is spent freeing itself with a strikes-last penalty.
parameters: {"consequence": "target counts as knocked down", "escape_test": "Strength", "hit": "ballistic skill", "recovery": "next recovery phase, cuts free and strikes last"}
notes: _netter resolves the ballistic-skill hit and the Strength escape test and leaves the target KNOCKED_DOWN; the automatic hit follows from the knocked-down helpless path and the wound roll is kept. The free-itself recovery and the strikes-last penalty are delivered by the ordinary knocked-down/stood-up handling of the standing-up rules that the clause itself cites.

clause_text: If he misses or the target escapes then the goblin makes a failed charge. If the failed charge would take him into base contact then stop him 1" away.
semantic_contract: A missed or escaped net charge is a failed charge that stops 1" short instead of reaching base contact. Closure: unmodelled while charge movement and distances stay outside the duelling model.
notes: Charge movement and distances are excluded from the 1v1 duelling model, so no operator is required and none exists; the individual combat consequence of the net is analysed in the whole-rule clause.

clause_text: Each natural hit roll of six grants another attack; further natural sixes generate further attacks.
semantic_contract: Each natural hit roll of six grants another attack, and further natural sixes generate further attacks. Closure: a natural six on a To Hit roll appends one more attack with the same weapon to the same pool, and the chain continues for as long as sixes are rolled.
parameters: {"effect": "one further attack", "trigger": "each natural hit roll of six"}
notes: _resolve_attack_pool re-queues the weapon when the hit roll is a natural six and iterates the growing list, so successive sixes generate successive attacks inside the same collective preparation; the tag is also flagged as requiring the modular engine for optimized ports (port limit, not a semantic gap).

clause_text: Retains the first-round Strength bonus of Flails and Morning Stars in later rounds.
semantic_contract: The bearer keeps the first-round Strength bonus of Flails and Morning Stars in later rounds. Closure: with this rule a flail or morning star adds its printed first-round Strength bonus in every round, not only the first.
notes: _attack_strength adds weapon.first_round_strength_bonus whenever the weapon carries the flail or morning-star tag and the rule is present, independently of the first-round flag. This consumes the same term the weapon profile carries, so no second contribution is added.

clause_text: When the mounted Knight charges, if he has at least 1 other model within 2 inches, all friendly charging mounted warriors (including the Questing Knight) within 4 inches gain +1 to Hit, cause fear and are immune to all Psychology for the first round of combat.
semantic_contract: When the mounted Knight charges, he gains +1 To Hit, causes fear and is immune to all Psychology for the first round of combat. Closure: a mounted Bitter Moors recipient that charges is compiled with +1 to hit, causes-fear and psychology immunity for the first round.
notes: compile_fighter only emits condition.righteous-charge for a mounted recipient (refusing otherwise and refusing a non-Bitter-Moors package), prepare_hit_context adds +1 for the condition/mechanic tag and the psychology and fear paths honour the immunity tags. The individual consequence supplied with the entry is therefore delivered.

clause_text: If he has at least 1 other model within 2 inches, all friendly charging mounted warriors (including the Questing Knight) within 4 inches gain +1 to Hit, cause fear and are immune to all Psychology for the first round of combat.
semantic_contract: The aura requires friendly models within 2 inches and spreads to friendly charging mounted warriors within 4 inches. Closure: unmodelled while the duel supplies exactly two combatants and no friendly models or distances.
notes: Groups and independent third combatants are excluded from the duelling model, so the aura cannot trigger and needs no operator; the self-buff part of the same printed rule is analysed in the whole-rule clause.

clause_text: Sabretusks fight with two attacks instead of one during the turn they charge.
semantic_contract: Sabretusks fight with two attacks instead of one during the turn they charge. Closure: on the charging turn the base attack count is 2 rather than the profile 1, and in later rounds it returns to the profile value.
notes: build_attacks substitutes base_characteristic = 2 when charging with the sabretusk tag, which is the printed replacement of A1 by A2 rather than a generic bonus; the substitution is scoped to the charging context.

clause_text: The Amazon has learned to channel her anger and aggression making her a veritable animal while attacking her foes. Any Amazon model with this skill receives + 1 A when charging and is immune to charm effects and fear.
semantic_contract: An Amazon with this skill receives +1 Attack when charging and is immune to charm effects and fear. Closure: a charged attack pool carries one extra attack and charm and fear effects never take hold on the bearer.
notes: build_attacks consumes charge_attacks_bonus (the tag is carried by the global effect), the mesmerising-dance and mark-of-shornaal gates honour mechanic.charm-immunity and the leadership and psychology paths honour mechanic.fear-immunity, so both the bonus and both printed immunities are delivered.

clause_text: Rolls D6+1 Attacks again at the start of every close-combat phase.
semantic_contract: The spawn rolls its attacks again at the start of every close-combat phase, gaining 1D6+1 attacks. Closure: at the start of each round the spawn attack count is rolled as D6+1 before the pool is built.
notes: resolve_spawn_attack_count rolls D6+1 per round and supplies it as base_attacks; the only printed exception found in the source (the vomit replacement) is excluded from the reroll by the same function.

clause_text: Whenever an enemy fails a To Hit roll against the Hero, or the Hero successfully parries an attack, that enemy suffers a cumulative -1 Initiative penalty until it is no longer engaged with the Hero or the Hero is taken Out of Action. The penalty can reduce Initiative to 0.
semantic_contract: Whenever an enemy fails a To Hit roll against the Hero, or the Hero successfully parries an attack, that enemy suffers a cumulative -1 Initiative penalty until it is no longer engaged with the Hero or the Hero is taken out of action, and the penalty can reduce Initiative to 0. Closure: each miss and each successful parry adds one point of Initiative penalty to that enemy, the penalty persists while engaged and can drive the final Initiative to 0.
parameters: {"ends": "no longer engaged or the Hero out of action", "initiative_penalty": "-1 cumulative, floor 0", "trigger": "enemy misses or the Hero parries"}
notes: _resolve_reference_attack_once adds initiative_penalty + 1 and sets initiative_floor = 0 both on a missed hit and on the parried branch, compared against the defender carrying the rule; resolve_priority subtracts the penalty and floors the result at the context floor. The printed persistence is the per-engagement state the duel carries for its two fighters.

clause_text: The Hero always strikes first in close combat when fighting any type of Skink, regardless of the weapon used or which model charged.
semantic_contract: The Hero always strikes first in close combat when fighting any type of Skink, regardless of the weapon used or which model charged. Closure: against a Skink profile the Hero resolves before the opponent in every round, whatever the weapon priority or charge state.
notes: resolve_priority raises the value to 20 for the always variant, which outranks charge, weapon priority and strike-first values, matching "regardless of the weapon used or which model charged".

clause_text: Always strikes first in the first combat round against Skink profiles.
semantic_contract: Always strikes first in the first combat round against Skink profiles. Closure: against a Skink the priority spike applies in the first round and the ordinary order returns afterwards.
notes: resolve_priority applies the 20 value only in the first round for the first-round variant, returning to the ordinary weapon and Initiative order afterwards.

clause_text: The hero is titanic in size and muscle mass. Whenever this Brood member hits an enemy warrior, but fails to wound, the hit model must pass a Strength test to avoid getting knocked down.
semantic_contract: Whenever this Brood member hits an enemy warrior but fails to wound, the hit model must pass a Strength test or be knocked down. Closure: a hit whose To Wound roll fails forces a Strength test on the defender and a failed test leaves it Knocked Down.
conditions: {"trigger": "failed To Wound roll after a hit"}
notes: _resolve_reference_attack_once runs the titanic-strength branch after a failed wound, rolling a Strength test (with the blessed-sight reroll honoured) and setting KNOCKED_DOWN on failure.

clause_text: The Hero may declare one of its attacks Unpredictable; that attack cannot be parried by the opponent.
semantic_contract: The Hero may declare one of its attacks Unpredictable and that attack cannot be parried. Closure: the declared attack is refused a parry attempt while the remaining attacks stay parryable.
parameters: {"cannot_be_parried": true, "selection": "one declared attack", "declaration_input": "unresolved: the route always applies it to the first allocated attack"}
notes: _resolve_attack_pool marks weapons[0] with cannot_be_parried whenever the tag is present, so the effect is delivered but the printed declaration is not modelled: the first allocated attack is always the unparryable one and no choice of which attack is offered. With two weapons the difference is observable, so the missing selection is recorded as a behaviour gap rather than as a satisfied clause. Correction round: the delivered half and the exact violation point. pools._resolve_attack_pool merges cannot_be_parried into weapons[0] only, so exactly one attack of the pool is refused a parry, but the printed declaration is not modelled: the affected attack is always the first allocated one and no input chooses it. Distinguishing example: a Hero with a main axe and an off-hand sword facing a defender with one parry - printed: the Hero may declare the sword attack unpredictable and let the parry face the axe; current: the axe attack is always the unparryable one and the defender parries the sword attack.

clause_text: Whenever a Wheelo moves into a model, that model automatically suffers 1D3 Strength 4 hits, which are worked out before any blows are struck, in the same way as a crossbow pistol. These represent the Impact Hits of the Wheelo as it comes to a sudden stop against an unsolid object. These are only dealt in the first round of combat, and only if the Wheelo "charged" this turn. Models that charge a Wheelo during his or her turn do NOT suffer Impact Hits. If a Wheelo rolls into a friendly model, that model still suffers Impact Hits as normal. An Impact Hit does not reflect the strength of the Wheelo crew, and thus the attack will remain S4, even if the crew gains a Strength Upgrade.
semantic_contract: When a Wheelo moves into a model that model automatically suffers 1D3 Strength 4 hits worked out before any blows are struck, only in the first round of combat and only if the Wheelo charged; the attack stays S4 even if the crew gains a Strength upgrade. Closure: a charging Wheelo resolves 1D3 automatic, unparryable Strength 4 hits before the attack pools of that round.
notes: resolve_round resolves the collision block before the strike sequence, deriving the count from the printed D3, using an effect with automatic_hit, cannot_be_parried and a fixed Strength 4 (or 5 for the morning-star fitting), and stripping the crew global effects so no Strength upgrade reaches the hits.

clause_text: Models that charge a Wheelo during his or her turn do NOT suffer Impact Hits. If a Wheelo rolls into a friendly model, that model still suffers Impact Hits as normal.
semantic_contract: A model that charges the Wheelo takes no Impact Hits, while any model the Wheelo rolls into does, friend or not. Closure: the collision block only runs for the Wheelo owner charging (or for the single spear-fitted retaliatory hit) and never for an ordinary charger.
notes: The collision loop runs for (charging or counter) and the counter only exists for the spear fitting, so an ordinary charger never suffers Impact Hits. The friendly-model sentence is a group clause that cannot arise with two opposing combatants; it is noted here rather than spun into a separate excluded row.

clause_text: Weapons Training: as Wheelos do not carry weapons as such (any blades etc. on the Wheelo itself count as the instruments for the actual Impact Hits themselves). However, a Wheelo who gains "Weapons Training" may have one of the following weapons fitted to its body. This will boost the Impact Hits in the following way: Axe - Impact Hits deal -1 Armour save. Club - Impact Hits deal Concussion. Spear - if charged, the Wheelo still deals a single Impact Hit to the charger before attacks are made. Morning Star - the first round of Impact Hits dealt each game are at S5 instead of S4; all Impact Hits after are at normal Strength. Sprint: instead of rolling 2D6" to run/charge, the Snotling player may choose to move the Wheelo 3D6" instead. Mighty Blow: the crew gains +1 to wound in combat; has no effect on Impact Hits.
semantic_contract: A Wheelo with Weapons Training may fit one of the listed weapons, boosting its Impact Hits: an axe adds -1 armour save, a club adds Concussion, a spear adds one Impact Hit against a charger, and a morning star makes the first round of Impact Hits S5; the crew Mighty Blow swap gives +1 to wound in combat with no effect on Impact Hits, and Sprint allows 3D6" movement instead of 2D6". Closure: each fitting changes exactly the printed term on the Impact Hit or crew attack and leaves the others untouched.
parameters: {"axe": "Impact Hits -1 armour save", "club": "Impact Hits Concussion", "fittings": ["axe", "club", "spear", "morning-star", "sprint", "mighty-blow"], "mighty-blow": "crew +1 to wound in combat, no effect on Impact Hits", "morning-star": "first round of Impact Hits at S5", "spear": "single Impact Hit when charged", "sprint": "3D6 movement"}
notes: compile_fighter refuses a fitting without a Wheelo and emits the wheelo.fitting.<x> tags; the impact block reads them for armour penetration (axe), concussion (club), the single retaliatory hit (spear, gated on the opponent charging) and the first S5 impact (morning star, spent once); the mighty-blow swap replaces the ordinary +1 Strength with +1 to wound and the Impact Hit effect keeps its fixed Strength, which is the printed "has no effect on Impact Hits".

clause_text: Sprint: instead of rolling 2D6" to run/charge, the Snotling player may choose to move the Wheelo 3D6" instead.
semantic_contract: Sprint changes the run/charge movement distance from 2D6" to 3D6". Closure: unmodelled while charge and run distances stay outside the duelling model.
notes: Charge and run distance is a movement subsystem excluded from the 1v1 duelling scope; no operator is required and none exists. The combat fittings of the same printed rule are analysed in the whole-rule clause.

clause_text: Attacks use Strength 4 without modifying enemy armour saves.
semantic_contract: Wolf Rat bites use Strength 4 without modifying enemy armour saves. Closure: the wound roll uses S4 while the armour save is calculated from S3, so no extra armour modifier is produced.
notes: _attack_strength raises the bite to the printed S4 (matching the wolf-rat-bite branch that keeps a separate armour Strength) so the wound roll uses 4 while prepare_armour_context keeps the armour modifier of the unmodified Strength, which is exactly the printed "without modifying enemy armour saves".

clause_text: The hero may make a Wraith Touch attack instead of their normal attacks in close combat. The hero making a Wraith Touch makes a single unarmed attack, if it hits, it wounds automatically, all rules that apply to unarmed attacks apply to the Wraith Touch. If a Liche uses this skill and wounds, then he may regain one lost wound. This may not take the hero beyond his starting total. Necromancers do not regain wounds with this skill. This skill has no effect on the Possessed or Undead.
semantic_contract: Instead of their normal attacks the hero may make a single unarmed Wraith Touch attack that wounds automatically, with all unarmed rules applying; a Liche that wounds regains one lost wound without exceeding his starting total, Necromancers do not, and the skill has no effect on the Possessed or Undead. Closure: the replacement pool is one unarmed attack that wounds automatically against eligible defenders, the Liche heal is capped at the starting total and an Undead or Possessed defender takes the ordinary attack instead.
parameters: {"attacks": 1, "family": "undead/necromantic", "hit_effect": "wounds automatically", "immune_targets": ["Possessed", "Undead"], "regain": "one wound (Liche only)", "scope": "instead of normal attacks", "weapon": "unarmed"}
notes: select_attack_replacement offers the wraith-touch replacement, build_attacks clamps the pool to one, _resolve_attack_pool and prepare_wound_context grant the automatic wound only against non-undead, non-possessed defenders and the Liche heal is the wraith-touch branch of the wound damage resolution. The replacement is refused on the optimized ports (port limit, not a semantic gap).

clause_text: The Wardancer rains blow after blow upon their opponent, moving with such speed that the eye cannot follow each distinct cut and thrust. While performing this Dance, a warrior is granted +1 Attack.
semantic_contract: While performing this Dance the warrior is granted +1 Attack. Closure: while Storm of Blades is the selected dance the attack pool carries exactly one extra attack.
conditions: {"effect": "attacks_bonus 1", "repeat": "not the dance used in the previous phase", "selection": "one dance per phase", "trigger": "combat phase start"}
notes: select_shadow_dance adds attacks_bonus 1 to the global effect, which build_attacks consumes. The selection itself is the project composition of "while performing this Dance": one dance per combat phase, never the dance used in the previous phase, and a Wardancer must choose (the selector raises otherwise).

clause_text: With agile grace the Wardancer evades the clumsy attacks of their enemies, becoming almost impossible to strike. While performing this Dance, the Wardancer has a special 4+ save throw which cannot be modified by Strength, magic spells or magic weapons.
semantic_contract: While performing this Dance the Wardancer has a special 4+ save that cannot be modified by Strength, magic spells or magic weapons. Closure: the selected dance gives a 4+ special save that no Strength or magic term can worsen.
conditions: {"effect": "special save 4+", "repeat": "not the dance used in the previous phase", "selection": "one dance per phase", "trigger": "combat phase start"}
notes: select_shadow_dance adds the dance.shadows-coil-active tag and prepare_special_save_context turns it into a 4+ save; the special-save context is not parameterised by Strength, magic or magic weapons, so the printed "cannot be modified" is structural rather than a second modifier term.

clause_text: Each strike of the Wardancer's blade is made with uncanny precision, capable of severing a head or piercing a heart with one deceptively elegant stroke. While performing this Dance, the warrior gains +1 to any Injury rolls.
semantic_contract: While performing this Dance the warrior gains +1 to any Injury rolls. Closure: while Whirling Death is the selected dance every Injury roll caused by that fighter carries one extra point.
conditions: {"effect": "injury_modifier 1", "repeat": "not the dance used in the previous phase", "selection": "one dance per phase", "trigger": "combat phase start"}
notes: select_shadow_dance raises the global injury_modifier by one, which the wound-damage path consumes when the Injury roll is made; no second contribution is added by the dance tag itself.

clause_text: The sinuous movements of this Dance distract and confuse the enemy, allowing the Wardancer to strike before their foe can react. When performing this Dance, the warrior reduces his total attacks by one but always Strikes first in combat. If their opponent also Strikes first, resolve attacks in Initiative order.
semantic_contract: When performing this Dance the warrior reduces his total attacks by one but always strikes first in combat; if the opponent also strikes first the attacks are resolved in Initiative order. Closure: the selected dance removes exactly one attack from the pool, raises the fighter to the strike-first tier and leaves simultaneous strike-first cases to the Initiative comparison.
conditions: {"effect": "attacks -1 and strike first", "repeat": "not the dance used in the previous phase", "selection": "one dance per phase", "trigger": "combat phase start"}
notes: build_attacks subtracts one for dance.woven-mist-active and resolve_priority raises the value to at least the strike-first tier for the same tag. "Resolve attacks in Initiative order" is the ordinary priority comparison: the tie is broken by Initiative (and an unbiased roll only on an exact tie), which is the shared combat-order operator rather than a second dance-specific term.

clause_text: Strikes first in close combat.
semantic_contract: The fighter strikes first in close combat. Closure: the bearer resolves before an ordinary opponent and the standing-up penalty cannot push him below the strike-first tier.
notes: The contract carries priority 1 for the tag and resolve_priority also treats the skill as the explicit strike-first override for a warrior who stood up, which is the only printed effect of the rule.

clause_text: The Hero may fight with bare claws without penalty and counts as using two close-combat weapons, gaining +1 Attack. In close combat, it scores a critical hit on a 'to wound' roll of 5-6 instead of only 6. When combined with Eshin Fighting Claws, this grants +2 Attacks instead of +1.
semantic_contract: The Hero may fight with bare claws or feet without penalty and counts as using two close-combat weapons, gaining +1 Attack. Closure: with a fist or fighting claws as the main weapon the unarmed penalty is waived and the pool carries one extra attack.
notes: Split from the former aggregate whole row so the three independently resolved consequences stand alone. ignores_unarmed_penalties lists the skill tag and build_attacks adds +1 when the main weapon is a fist or fighting claws, so the unarmed penalty waiver and the extra attack are delivered for both profiles.

clause_text: In close combat, it scores a critical hit on a 'to wound' roll of 5-6 instead of only 6.
semantic_contract: In close combat a To Wound roll of 5 or 6 is a critical wound instead of only 6. Closure: the wound context sets the critical threshold to 5 while the bearer has the skill tag, and the ordinary target < 6 guard still applies.
notes: prepare_wound_context lowers the threshold to 5 whenever the skill tag is present. Unlike the adjacent unarmed-critical-strikes term, which additionally requires weapon.fist, the art-of-silent-death term carries no fist/claw guard, so the improvement reaches any close-combat weapon. That matches the printed "in close combat" wording, and the fist-only guard that belongs to the separate skill is not claimed here.

clause_text: When combined with Eshin Fighting Claws, this grants +2 Attacks instead of +1.
semantic_contract: With Eshin Fighting Claws the skill contributes two attacks rather than one. Closure: the pool built with fighting claws carries one further attack than the same pool built with fists.
notes: The claw closing condition is met. build_attacks adds the same single skill attack for fists and for fighting claws, and the paired fighting-claw profile supplies the further attack through extra_weapon_attack, so the claw pool ends one attack higher. An isolated probe with Attacks 1 gave two fist attacks and three claw attacks (controls one and two), one further with claws. The earlier note that called this a claw-specific behaviour gap read only the +1 branch and ignored the paired contribution.

clause_text: Re-rolls missed axe attacks when charging.
semantic_contract: The fighter re-rolls missed axe attacks when charging. Closure: when charging with an axe or dwarf axe, failed To Hit rolls are re-rolled in the first round.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll for charging and first_round with an axe or dwarf-axe tag, refusing the reroll for any other weapon of the same fighter.

clause_text: The Slayer may add +1 to his close combat to hit rolls during the turn which he charges (may not be used with Ferocious Charge).
semantic_contract: The Slayer may add +1 to his close-combat To Hit rolls during the turn in which he charges, and may not use it together with Ferocious Charge. Closure: a charging turn grants +1 to hit, and the bonus never applies in the same turn as the Ferocious Charge doubling.
notes: contexts.prepare_hit_context adds the +1 to hit for a charging attacker carrying skill.berserker, so the bonus half is delivered. The printed exclusivity with Ferocious Charge is a construction rule, not a missing runtime term: the Troll Slayer package binds compiler.berserker-incompatible-with-ferocious-charge (listed in contracts.COMPILER_CONTRACTS), and the shared eligibility loadout restriction (typescript/domain/eligibility/index.ts::skillLoadoutRestriction, mirrored in mordheim_construction/_eligibility.js) refuses a build that also carries skill.ferocious-charge with 'Berserker may not be combined with Ferocious Charge'. A compiled fighter therefore never holds both tags, and the +1 is always applied under the printed exclusion; no runtime check is owed.

clause_text: The Augur may re-roll failed characteristic tests and failed rolls to hit in close combat or shooting; the second result must be accepted. If she was not taken Out of Action, she rolls two dice for her contribution during Exploration and may choose either die as the result.
semantic_contract: The Augur may re-roll failed characteristic tests and failed To Hit rolls in close combat or shooting, accepting the second result. Closure: with the skill every failed characteristic test and every missed To Hit roll may be taken again once, and the second result stands.
notes: The contract carries reroll_hits, which _hit_reroll ORs into the hit reroll, and the aftermath characteristic tests (contagious, force of will, fire recovery and others) pass the blessed-sight tag as the reroll argument. The Exploration dice belong to the campaign subsystem and are not part of the duel.

clause_text: If she was not taken Out of Action, she rolls two dice for her contribution during Exploration and may choose either die as the result.
semantic_contract: The post-battle Exploration contribution uses two dice with the better result chosen. Closure: unmodelled while campaign acquisition and Exploration stay outside the duelling model.
notes: Campaign acquisition is an explicit exclusion of this block, so no duel operator is required; the in-duel rerolls of the same printed rule are analysed in the whole-rule clause.

clause_text: Experts with pistols in close quarters; they have an uncanny ability to turn what should have missed its target into a success. When using pistols in close combat, they may re-roll any missed to-hit rolls with the pistol in the first round of combat.
semantic_contract: When using pistols in close combat the fighter may re-roll any missed To Hit rolls with the pistol in the first round of combat. Closure: a first-round close-combat pistol attack re-rolls its misses.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll for first_round with a pistol or duelling-pistol tag; the pistol attack itself is the first-round pistol profile that equipment_for_state keeps only for that round.

clause_text: In the first melee round, enemies in base contact test Leadership and miss their first attack on failure, even their only attack.
semantic_contract: In the first melee round, enemies in base contact test Leadership and miss their first attack on failure, even their only attack. Closure: in the first round the opponent tests Leadership and a failure removes exactly its first attack from the pool while the remaining attacks still resolve.
parameters: {"consequence": "first attack lost on failure", "frequency": "first melee round", "test": "Leadership"}
notes: resolve_crude_belch runs in the first round for both sides, takes the Leadership test (honouring both Leadership paths) and sets the timed first-attack loss that the pool then honours. The function raises for additional enemy contacts, which is the printed base-contact scope in a duel of exactly two combatants.

clause_text: Attacks cannot be parried.
semantic_contract: Attacks made by this fighter cannot be parried. Closure: a parry attempt against the bearer is refused while ordinary hits stay parryable for the opponent.
notes: The contract carries cannot_be_parried, which resolve_parry tests against the defender eligibility so no parry dice are rolled against the bearer. The effect belongs to the fighter rather than one weapon, matching the printed wording "attacks cannot be parried".

clause_text: If the Saurus Slayer is engaged with only a single opponent in melee, he may re-roll missed hits in the first round whether he charged or was charged.
semantic_contract: If the Saurus Slayer is engaged with only a single opponent in melee he may re-roll missed hits in the first round whether he charged or was charged. Closure: in the first round, with one engaged opponent, missed hits are re-rolled regardless of who charged.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll for first_round with the duellist tag and does not test the charge direction, which is the printed "whether he charged or was charged"; a duel always supplies exactly one opponent, which is the printed single-opponent requirement.

clause_text: +1 to wound rolls.
semantic_contract: The fighter adds +1 to wound rolls. Closure: every To Wound roll made by the bearer carries one extra point.
notes: The wound context adds the printed wound_modifier 1 from the global effect before comparing with the printed To Wound table.

clause_text: Swordsmen are so skilled with their weapons that they may re-roll any failed hits when charging. Note that this only applies when they are armed with normal swords, and not with doublehanded swords or any other weapons.
semantic_contract: Swordsmen may re-roll any failed hits when charging, and this applies only when armed with normal swords, not with double-handed swords or other weapons. Closure: the charging reroll is granted for a sword and refused for a double-handed sword or any other weapon.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll only for charging, first_round with a weapon.sword or weapon.weeping-blades tag; a double-handed sword does not carry the sword tag, so the printed exclusion is effect-tag driven rather than a name test, and the weeping-blades annotation is the source ruling already recorded for that item.

clause_text: Adds one Attack to the profile.
semantic_contract: Adds one Attack to the profile. Closure: the attack profile carries one more attack than the printed characteristic.
notes: attacks_bonus 1 is summed into the pool before the doubling and extra-weapon terms, which is the printed profile addition.

clause_text: The Slayer may double his attacks on the turn in which he charges. He will suffer a –1 to hit penalty on that turn.
semantic_contract: The Slayer may double his attacks on the turn in which he charges and suffers -1 to hit on that turn. Closure: a charging turn doubles the pool (before the second-weapon attack is added) and applies one point of to-hit penalty.
notes: build_attacks doubles the pool for a charging first round with the tag, before the extra-weapon attack is added, and prepare_hit_context subtracts one for the same tag and turn, matching both printed terms.

clause_text: Knocked Down results caused by the warrior become Stunned.
semantic_contract: Knocked Down results caused by the warrior become Stunned. Closure: an injury result that would leave the opponent Knocked Down is upgraded to Stunned when it was caused by the bearer.
notes: _injury_context passes head_crusher into the injury condition, which upgrades the knocked-down band to stunned; the flag is attached to the attacking effect, so only results caused by that fighter are upgraded.

clause_text: The Vampire may re-roll failed To Hit rolls during the turn in which it charges.
semantic_contract: The Vampire may re-roll failed To Hit rolls during the turn in which it charges. Closure: a charging turn grants the hit reroll and later rounds do not.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll for charging, first_round with the infallible tag and no other tag of the same fighter receives it.

clause_text: Retains the Strength bonus of heavy weapons.
semantic_contract: The fighter retains the Strength bonus of heavy weapons. Closure: the printed first-round Strength bonus of a flail or morning star applies in every round for this bearer.
notes: _attack_strength adds the weapon first_round_strength_bonus whenever the mighty-biceps tag is on the effect, independently of the first-round flag, which is the printed retention of the heavy-weapon bonus.

clause_text: +1 Strength in close combat, excluding pistols.
semantic_contract: The fighter adds +1 Strength in close combat, excluding pistols. Closure: attack Strength rises by one for close-combat weapons while a pistol attack receives no Strength bonus from this skill.
notes: contexts._attack_strength computes strength = effect.fixed_strength or state.strength + effect.strength_bonus, and the bound weapon.pistol profile declares fixed_strength 4, so a pistol attack keeps Strength 4 and the global strength_bonus 1 from skill.mighty-blow never reaches it; the printed pistol exclusion is delivered by the common strength formula rather than by a pistol-specific gate. An axe attack by the same fighter takes the additive branch and does gain the +1.

clause_text: Uses the effective Strength needed to wound on 4+ when calculating the armour-save modifier.
semantic_contract: The fighter uses the effective Strength needed to wound on 4+ when calculating the armour-save modifier. Closure: the armour modifier is computed from the effective Strength of the attack rather than from the raw profile Strength.
notes: prepare_armour_context substitutes the effective monster-slayer Strength for the armour calculation while the wound roll keeps the printed maximum of 4, which is the two-part monster-slayer reading recorded for this entry; the contract tags the variant once so it adds no second contribution.

clause_text: +1 Wound.
semantic_contract: The fighter gains +1 Wound. Closure: the bearer starts the duel with one more wound than the printed characteristic and the maximum it can recover to includes that extra wound.
notes: The duel state builds the starting wounds from the characteristic plus one for the monstrous tag, and the revenant recovery maximum uses the same sum, so the added wound is delivered and cannot be exceeded by healing.

clause_text: The Vampire gains +1 Attack. This does not count toward its normal characteristic maximum.
semantic_contract: The Vampire gains +1 Attack and this does not count toward its normal characteristic maximum. Closure: the pool carries one extra attack while the printed characteristic maximum is untouched.
notes: attacks_bonus 1 is summed separately from the characteristic, so the printed "does not count toward the characteristic maximum" is structural: the bonus never enters the characteristic value, which is the only consumer the campaign maximum would look at.

clause_text: The bearer hates all Skaven, Undead, Possessed, Beastmen, Dark Elves and other warbands classed as evil. Non-Chaos human warbands whose members are merely killers or looters are not included.
semantic_contract: The bearer hates all Skaven, Undead, Possessed, Beastmen, Dark Elves and other warbands classed as evil, but not non-Chaos human warbands whose members are merely killers or looters. Closure: against a listed species, an evil warband or a chaos follower the first-round hit reroll applies, and a merely human warband never triggers it.
parameters: {"excludes": "non-Chaos human killers or looters", "first_round": true, "reroll": "failed hits", "targets": ["Skaven", "Undead", "Possessed", "Beastmen", "Dark Elves", "evil warbands"]}
conditions: {"exclusion": "plain human warbands", "target_scope": "listed species or evil alignment", "trigger": "first round"}
notes: _hit_reroll resolves righteous fury through the explicit species set (skaven, undead, possessed, beastman, dark-elf), the chaotic warband-group and chaos-follower identities, and the evil warband group only when the human and human-mercenary groups are absent, which is exactly the printed exclusion. The reroll is scoped to the first round as hatred is.

clause_text: Gains an additional attack at the user's Strength; armour is modified normally according to that Strength.
semantic_contract: The fighter gains an additional attack at his own Strength, with armour modified normally according to that Strength. Closure: with a shield in the off hand the pool carries one further attack resolved at the bearer Strength with the ordinary armour modifier of that Strength.
notes: compile_fighter appends the extra attack tagged rule.shield-strike only when the off hand is a shield; the pool then resolves it with the ordinary strength and armour contexts, so the printed "armour is modified normally according to that Strength" is the shared armour computation rather than a second term.

clause_text: The halfling gains a bonus attack when charged that strikes first.
semantic_contract: The halfling gains a bonus attack when charged that strikes first. Closure: when charged, the halfling pool carries one more attack and that attack resolves at the strike-first tier.
notes: resolve_round detects the charged halfling and selects the shifty weapon, the extra attack joins the pool and the priority of that attack is resolved at the strike-first tier; require_optimized_support refuses the tag for optimized ports, which is a port limit rather than a semantic gap.

clause_text: The Vampire gains +1 Strength during the turn in which it charges. This does not count toward its normal characteristic maximum.
semantic_contract: The Vampire gains +1 Strength during the turn in which it charges, and this does not count toward its normal characteristic maximum. Closure: a charging turn adds one point of attack Strength and later rounds return to the printed profile.
notes: _attack_strength adds the charge_strength_bonus only when first_round and charging, which is the printed charging turn; the bonus stays outside the characteristic, so the "does not count toward the maximum" rider is structural.

clause_text: +1 to Injury rolls caused in close combat.
semantic_contract: The fighter adds +1 to Injury rolls caused in close combat. Closure: every close-combat Injury roll caused by the bearer carries one extra point.
notes: The injury context sums the printed injury_modifier 1 into the injury roll, so every close-combat injury result caused by that fighter is raised by the same point; shooting injuries are outside this block.

clause_text: Blackguards are capable of great feats of strength. They may use a double-handed weapon without the usual penalty of always striking last. Work out the order of battle as you would with other weapons.
semantic_contract: The fighter may use a double-handed weapon without the usual penalty of always striking last, working out the order of battle as with other weapons. Closure: with a two-handed weapon or broadsword the bearer is not pushed to the strike-last tier and stands in the ordinary order.
notes: resolve_priority cancels the negative weapon priority when the strongman flag and a two-handed or broadsword weapon are present, and the same condition is used when the optimized plan is compiled, so the printed exception reaches both engines.

clause_text: Re-rolls failed wound rolls.
semantic_contract: The fighter re-rolls failed wound rolls. Closure: a failed To Wound roll may be taken again once and the second result stands.
notes: The contract carries reroll_wounds, which the wound resolution consumes as the printed re-roll of a failed To Wound roll; the re-rolled die is a single further attempt, not a second effect.

clause_text: With a double-handed weapon, replaces all attacks with one automatic hit if the opponent fails an Initiative test.
semantic_contract: With a double-handed weapon the fighter replaces all attacks with one automatic hit if the opponent fails an Initiative test. Closure: with a double-handed weapon in hand the pool is one attack that hits without a To Hit roll and only when the Initiative test fails.
notes: build_attacks clamps the pool to one for a two-handed sweep and the attack resolution runs the printed Initiative test before granting the automatic hit, so both the replacement and the pass condition are delivered.

clause_text: Unarmed attacks score critical hits on To Wound rolls of 5-6.
semantic_contract: Unarmed attacks score critical hits on To Wound rolls of 5-6. Closure: a To Wound roll of 5 or 6 with the fists is a critical wound while a 6 required to wound still denies it.
notes: prepare_wound_context lowers the critical threshold to 5 for unarmed attacks carrying this skill, and the ordinary target-under-6 guard of the critical operator keeps the printed "unless a 6 is required" reading intact.

clause_text: Fights unarmed without penalties and gains +1 Attack while unarmed.
semantic_contract: The fighter fights unarmed without penalties and gains +1 Attack while unarmed. Closure: with the fists the pool is not clamped to one attack, the unarmed Strength and armour penalties are ignored and one extra attack is added.
notes: The skill is listed by ignores_unarmed_penalties, which removes the fist clamp in build_attacks, adds the printed extra attack, and both the Strength and the armour contexts consult the same helper so the dagger-like fist penalties disappear from the whole exchange.

clause_text: +1 WS when charging.
semantic_contract: The fighter gains +1 Weapon Skill when charging. Closure: a charging turn raises the attack Weapon Skill by one and later rounds return to the printed value.
notes: prepare_hit_context adds charge_ws_bonus to the attacker Weapon Skill for a first-round charge, which is the printed +1 WS for that turn.

clause_text: When fighting a model with a higher Strength characteristic, the warrior may re-roll failed hand-to-hand hit rolls.
semantic_contract: When fighting a model with a higher Strength characteristic the warrior may re-roll failed close-combat hit rolls. Closure: against an opponent whose printed Strength exceeds the bearer Strength, missed hits are re-rolled.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll for the virtue tag only when defender.characteristics.strength exceeds the attacker characteristic, so the comparison uses the printed characteristic rather than the effective Strength of the attack.

clause_text: Re-rolls failed hit rolls with an axe or double-handed weapon.
semantic_contract: The fighter re-rolls failed hit rolls with an axe or double-handed weapon. Closure: missed hits with an axe, dwarf axe or two-handed weapon are re-rolled in every round.
notes: _hit_reroll raises the reroll for the three weapon tags without a round or charge condition, matching the printed unconditional wording of the skill.

clause_text: +1 on close-combat Critical Hit tables.
semantic_contract: The fighter adds +1 on close-combat Critical Hit tables. Closure: a critical wound caused by the bearer rolls its critical result with one extra point of modifier.
notes: The critical resolution adds one to the modifier for the web-of-steel tag, on top of the printed critical_injury_bonus of materials such as the Dark Elf Blade, so the two printed modifiers remain separate additive terms.

clause_text: Re-rolls failed wound rolls against opponents with a strictly higher natural Strength.
semantic_contract: Re-rolls failed wound rolls against opponents with a strictly higher natural Strength. Closure: missed To Wound rolls are re-rolled only when the defender printed Strength is strictly greater than the bearer printed Strength.
notes: prepare_wound_context grants the reroll for the wound-valour tag when the defender natural Strength is strictly higher, so the printed comparison and its strictness are both carried by the operator.

clause_text: A natural 6 to hit guarantees a wound; an optional wound die can score a critical on 6, otherwise the wound remains normal. Normal critical eligibility and saves apply.
semantic_contract: A natural 6 to hit wounds automatically, and a wound die may still be rolled for that wound: a 6 makes it a critical hit, anything else leaves a normal wound, with armour saves taken as normal. Closure: a natural six to hit sets an automatic wound, the optional wound die decides between normal and critical, and the ordinary save steps still resolve.
notes: _resolve_reference_attack_once and the attack pool resolve the Lotus as an automatic wound on a natural six with an optional wound die whose six alone grants the critical, and prepare_wound_context keeps the Lotus out of the ordinary critical-threshold branches so the optional die is the only route to a critical.

clause_text: +1 S when wounding and calculating armour penetration.
semantic_contract: The poison adds +1 Strength when wounding and when calculating armour penetration. Closure: the wounded Strength is one point higher and the armour modifier uses that same raised Strength.
notes: The contract carries strength_bonus 1, which _attack_strength folds into the attack Strength, and prepare_armour_context derives the armour modifier from that same Strength, so the printed "and calculating armour penetration" is delivered by one term rather than two.

clause_text: Doubles wounds caused.
semantic_contract: The poison doubles the wounds caused. Closure: a Bloodroot wound inflicts two wounds, and combined with another multiple-wound effect the higher value is used instead of multiplying.
notes: The contract carries damage 2 and the wound-damage resolution takes max(1, weapon_damage, critical.damage), which is the printed doubling read together with the shared core rule that a doubling is never multiplied by another multiple-wound source.

clause_text: Re-rolls failed wound rolls; the re-roll cannot cause a critical hit.
semantic_contract: Failed wound rolls are re-rolled and the re-roll cannot cause a critical hit. Closure: a failed To Wound roll is taken again once and a successful re-roll counts as an ordinary wound whatever the die shows.
notes: The contract carries reroll_wounds, and the critical operator receives critical_on_reroll=False for this poison, which is the printed exclusion of a critical from the second roll.

clause_text: +1 to wound rolls; a natural 1 always fails.
semantic_contract: The poison adds +1 to wound rolls and a natural 1 always fails. Closure: every To Wound roll gains one point while a natural 1 still fails regardless of the modified target.
notes: prepare_wound_context adds the printed wound_modifier 1 and the attack resolution keeps the manbane natural-1 failure branch, so both printed halves are present.

clause_text: Each unsaved wound reduces the opponent’s Initiative by 1, to a minimum of 1.
semantic_contract: Each unsaved wound reduces the opponent Initiative by 1, to a minimum of 1. Closure: every wound that is not saved lowers the target Initiative by one and the printed minimum of 1 is respected.
notes: _resolve_wound_damage applies one point of nightshade Initiative penalty per point of damage that passes the saves, and resolve_priority subtracts the accumulated penalty after flooring the Initiative, which preserves the printed minimum of 1.

clause_text: +1 S when wounding, without increasing armour penetration.
semantic_contract: Reptile Venom is bought by Skink henchmen for their missile weapons, adds +1 Strength without the -1 save modifier, lasts one battle and requires the whole henchman group to be armed alike. Closure: no Reptile Venom term applies in a close-combat duel.
notes: The clarification F074-reptile-venom decides the poison is outside the duel (missile-only, one battle), so no duel contribution is admitted. No effect ID or consumer is claimed for the excluded clause; the contract parameters exist in the KB and are left untouched, and the row records the exclusion instead of silently treating the operator as an in-duel effect.

clause_text: An undefended hit immediately causes a Toughness test; failure paralyses the target, preventing attacks and granting automatic hits until it passes a test in its own Recovery phase.
semantic_contract: An undefended hit immediately forces a Toughness test; a failure paralyses the target, preventing its attacks and granting automatic hits against it, until it passes a test in its own Recovery phase. Closure: an unsaved hit sets a Toughness test, failure blocks the target attacks and makes hits against it automatic, and success in its own recovery phase ends the paralysis.
parameters: {"effects": ["cannot attack", "automatic hits against it"], "failure": "paralysed", "recovery": "own Recovery phase test", "test": "Toughness", "trigger": "undefended hit"}
notes: The attack resolution runs the spider-spittle paralysis on an undefended hit and the round recovery phase resolves the printed Toughness test that ends it; the automatic hits are the helpless-path behaviour of the blocked target.

clause_text: Causes critical hits on 5-6 unless a natural 6 is required to wound.
semantic_contract: The poison causes critical hits on 5-6 unless a natural 6 is required to wound. Closure: a To Wound roll of 5 or 6 sets a critical wound, and when the target is 6 no critical is possible.
parameters: {"critical_threshold": 5, "guard": "unless a natural 6 is required to wound"}
notes: prepare_wound_context lowers the critical threshold to 5 for wolfsbane while the critical operator still requires a rolled success with a target below 6, which is exactly the printed guard.

clause_text: No material modifier.
semantic_contract: The normal material adds no modifier to the attack. Closure: a weapon declared with the normal material carries no additional Strength, armour, Initiative or save term.
notes: The contract is an empty parameter set carrying only the material tag, so no modifier term is produced; the clause is recorded expressly rather than left as a default because the absence of a term is the printed rule.

clause_text: Adds a further -1 armour-save modifier.
semantic_contract: Gromril adds a further -1 armour-save modifier. Closure: a Gromril weapon reduces the target armour save by one point on top of the weapon own modifier.
notes: The contract carries armour_penetration 1, which prepare_armour_context adds to the printed Strength-based modifier; the item entry prints the same "+1 save modifier" wording so the material is additive as printed.

clause_text: +1 Initiative while the weapon is equipped.
semantic_contract: Ithilmar adds +1 Initiative while the weapon is equipped. Closure: a fighter with an Ithilmar weapon has one point more Initiative for the whole exchange in which the weapon is equipped.
notes: The contract carries initiative_bonus 1 and resolve_priority sums the weapon initiative bonus into the break tie term, which is the printed "while the weapon is equipped".

clause_text: +1 Strength for attacks made with the weapon.
semantic_contract: Obsidian adds +1 Strength for attacks made with the weapon. Closure: the attack Strength is one point higher while an Obsidian weapon is used.
notes: The contract carries strength_bonus 1 consumed by _attack_strength. The item entry prints the same "As user +1" reading plus bearer restrictions and a campaign recommendation, which belong to the eligibility and acquisition layers rather than to this attack clause.

clause_text: Re-rolls failed wound rolls.
semantic_contract: Dark Steel re-rolls failed wound rolls. Closure: a failed To Wound roll with a Dark Steel weapon is taken again once.
notes: The contract carries reroll_wounds, which the wound resolution consumes as the printed re-roll. The Trollheim item entry that binds this material carries no effect text at all, so the item-side text is a knowledge-data gap recorded with the item projection rather than a defect of this operator.

clause_text: Adds +1 to the critical hit table and treats Injury results of 2-4 as stunned; retains the underlying weapon's properties.
semantic_contract: The Dark Elf Blade adds +1 to the critical hit table and treats Injury results of 2-4 as stunned, while retaining the underlying weapon properties. Closure: a critical wound with the blade rolls its critical table with one extra point, an Injury total of 2-4 is Stunned and all other weapon properties stay unchanged.
notes: The contract carries critical_injury_bonus 1, which reaches resolve_critical, and concussion, which the injury condition consumes; the material merges with the weapon profile rather than replacing it, which is the printed "retains the underlying weapon properties".

clause_text: +1 S and +1D3 I for the entire battle.
semantic_contract: Crimson Shade grants +1 Strength and +1D3 Initiative for the entire battle. Closure: a duel fought under Crimson Shade raises attack Strength by one and Initiative by a rolled 1D3 for its whole duration.
notes: Correction round: the former finding that no Initiative term exists for this preparation is withdrawn. compiler.compile_fighter applies the duel_start/fighter effect set, so the tag reaches every runtime; state.initialize_fighter rolls the single 1D3 into the fighter state, resolve_round passes the delta to resolve_priority as initiative_bonus = state.initiative - characteristics.initiative, and _combined_effect/_attack_strength apply strength_bonus 1 to every close-combat attack. The native engine carries the same roll through the _compile_fighter crimson_shade flag and the vectorized engine through _new_state plus effective_initiative. Both printed terms of this canonical clause are delivered for the whole duel. The Undead/Possessed immunity is printed only on the item origin and is recorded as pending work there.

clause_text: A weapon coated with the sap of the Black Lotus will wound its target automatically if you roll a 6 to hit. Note that you can still roll a dice for every wound inflicted in this way. If you roll a 6, you will inflict a critical hit with that roll. If you do not roll a 6, you will cause a normal wound. Take armour saves as normal.
semantic_contract: Black Lotus: a natural 6 to hit wounds automatically, a wound die may be rolled for every wound inflicted in this way, a 6 makes that wound a critical hit and a non-6 leaves it normal, with armour saves taken as usual. Closure: one printed clause delivered by the shared Lotus operator, with the optional wound die deciding between a normal and a critical wound.
notes: This Trollheim item prints the fuller wording of the same clause as mechanic/poison.black-lotus and binds the same operator, so it adds no second runtime contribution; the duplicate reference is recorded here for traceability only.
